title: ID0382508 - DC/Si-D/FI -[MP / R7 170002231] Emergency stop button pressed error
description:
Reported behavior/issue:  Emergency stop button pressed error and IMD_BC3 and BC_4
Root cause:
Jumper cable was missing in emergency circuit. For bender issue, dispenser supply A- and B- were connected together.
Solution: Connect the jumper cable and rewire dispenser DC connections
On DAMEX Sanctioned List:Siemens
Warranty Status:Yes

additional_info.subject: Notes from RC
additional_info.body:
Charger show emergency stop error after installation on site. Emergency button is not pressed. All wiring are checked. Emergency button is checked with multimeter. All door switches are checked. When opening any door we get door opened error. When doors are closed we only get this emergency stop button pressed error in the screen of the charger and in SCB.
Also connection between the charger and dispenser was double checked by the electricians at the site.

additional_info.subject: ID0382508 - DC/Si-D/FI -[MP / R7 170002231] Emergency stop button pressed error CRM:00642001583
additional_info.body:
Hello Sakari,
Hope you are doing well.
Regarding the reported issue of a false emergency button pressed alarm, we have checked the charger from the backend and found it to be offline on SCB. Please refer to the attached picture for your reference.
We recommend following the steps below to troubleshoot the issue.
Trace the 24V Source:
Start from the QA26 input and trace the 24V power supply path backwards through the circuit.
Identify the origin of the 24V supply by examining each component and connection from the end point (QA26) to its source.
Component Examination:
Focus on the FA7 and FA8 components to determine their role in supplying 24V to QA26.
Verify the functionality of FA7 and FA8 to ensure they are operating correctly and supplying the required voltage
Voltage Check at XD34:19A:
Measure the voltage at XD34:19A.
If 24V is present at XD34:19A, this indicates that the sensors are closed, which implies that the doors are open.
If 24V is not present at XD34:19A, investigate potential issues with FA7 and FA8, as they may be causing the problem.
